$comment: Authored source for the content engine (Phase 8). This file contains PROSE and formula definitions only — never measurements. Every number a reader sees on /hazards/* is derived at build time by scripts/build_content_engine.mjs from committed artifacts (the forecast snapshot, the freshness artifact, and the event archive when one is loaded). The physics expressions are transcribed from scripts/physics_severity.py and are pinned by scripts/tests/test_content_engine.py against that module, so the copy cannot drift from the code it describes.

hazards.summary: Riverine and monsoon flooding, scored from how much rain falls and how hard it falls.

physics.note: Both terms are required and must be different quantities. The pipeline this project inherited passed the horizon total twice, which made a wet fortnight indistinguishable from a three-day burst; the corrected signature is pinned by scripts/tests/test_physics_severity.py.

hazards.model: The classifier labels the district-horizon unit from the same meteorological drivers (rainfall, temperature, wind, humidity, radiation, evapotranspiration). Its class and its severity index are separate outputs: the class says which hazard the drivers most resemble, the severity says how strong the resemblance is.
hazards.confidence: The published confidence is the model's own softmax over the eight classes and is reported as `uncalibrated_model_softmax`. It is not a probability of flooding and it is not derived from the physics cross-check.
limits: No hydrology: river levels, upstream release, embankment state and soil moisture are not inputs, so a high score means 'this much rain on this district', not 'this river will breach'.
The two rainfall classes (Flood and Flash Flood) share one physics proxy — distinguishing them needs drainage and terrain data the pipeline does not carry.

The soil-moisture channels in the current tensor are the fabricated constants this repository already flagged (`soil_channels_fabricated` on the snapshot); until a real ERA5-Land soil layer is wired in at the forecast timestep, the class is weaker than the rainfall alone would suggest.
sources: ERA5-Land daily aggregates (reanalysis, soil and radiation)
Sentinel-1 GRD (inundation context in the ETL, not in the live forecast path)

hazards.summary: Short-duration, high-intensity flooding — the burst case of the rainfall proxy.

physics.note: Identical to Flood in this implementation. The intensity term is what makes a burst score higher than a drizzle of the same total, but nothing in the proxy separates a flash flood from a slow one.

hazards.model: The classifier decides between Flood and Flash Flood from the driver tensor alone. On the committed snapshot the two classes are almost never both plausible for the same unit, and the physics track cannot arbitrate between them.
hazards.confidence: Same softmax caveat as Flood: uncalibrated, and published with that label.
limits: No terrain or drainage: catchments, slope and urban surfaces are absent, which is exactly what decides whether a burst becomes a flash flood.
Haor and hill-district flash floods are driven by upstream rainfall outside the district boundary; the drivers are district-aggregated.
A 24-hour peak inside a 15-day horizon is a coarse instrument for an event that lasts hours.
sources: FFWC bulletins (hydrological context, ingested as text)

hazards.season: April–May and October–November; the post-monsoon window is the more destructive
hazards.summary: Wind-driven coastal hazard — sustained wind above 50 km/h, with the rain it carries.

drivers: maximum sustained wind in the horizon (W, km/h)
physics.note: The 50 km/h floor means a calm week scores zero on the wind term regardless of rainfall.

hazards.model: The classifier reads the same drivers; the coastal districts concentrate the high scores because the drivers there are genuinely stronger, not because a coastal prior is applied.
hazards.confidence: Uncalibrated softmax, as above. A high confidence in Tropical Cyclone means the drivers resemble that class, not that a cyclone has been detected.
limits: No track, no storm structure, no surge: the hazard is inferred from district-aggregated weather, so landfall position and timing are not represented.
Storm surge — the main killer on the Bangladesh coast — depends on bathymetry and tide, neither of which is an input.

The 15-day horizon is inside the range where a numerical weather model still has skill for wind, but the boundary between 'cyclone remnant' and 'strong monsoon wind' is not something this proxy resolves.

hazards.season: November–April (dry season), most acute in the Barind and the south-west
hazards.summary: Heat load against the rainfall the horizon is expected to bring.

drivers: precipitation accumulated over the horizon (P_total, mm)
physics.note: The rainfall term is inverted: less rain scores higher. 200 mm is the reference total at which the rainfall component reaches zero.

hazards.model: Classified from the same drivers. Agricultural drought and meteorological drought are not distinguished — no soil-moisture or crop-stage input exists in the tensor.
hazards.confidence: Uncalibrated softmax. The confidence does not account for irrigation, which is what actually determines whether a dry fortnight damages a crop.
limits: No soil moisture, no irrigation, no crop calendar: this is meteorological dryness, not agricultural drought.
A dry horizon in the monsoon is a different event from a dry horizon in March; the proxy does not encode season.
MODIS NDVI/EVI and land-surface temperature exist in the ETL for the archive path but are not live inputs to the forecast.
sources: MODIS MOD13Q1 / MOD11A1 (vegetation and land-surface temperature in the ETL)

physics.note: The persistence term is the horizon length, not the number of consecutive hot days — a limitation of the current formula, stated here rather than papered over.

hazards.model: Classified from the same drivers; Heat Wave and Drought compete directly, since heat raises both scores.
hazards.confidence: Uncalibrated softmax. Humidity is a driver but wet-bulb temperature — the quantity that governs human heat stress — is not computed.
limits: Maximum temperature is a district aggregate: an urban heat island inside a district is invisible.
The persistence term cannot see consecutive days, so a long mild horizon and a short intense one can score alike.
Who is at risk (outdoor labour, the elderly, livestock) is a question this proxy does not touch.

hazards.season: December–February, concentrated in the north and north-west
hazards.summary: How far the minimum falls below 16 °C, plus persistence.

physics.note: 16 °C is the reference minimum at which the temperature term starts scoring; it is a formula constant, not a met-service threshold.

hazards.model: Classified from the same drivers; the districts that score highest are the ones where the minimum genuinely falls, not an a-priori cold-region list.
hazards.confidence: Uncalibrated softmax. Fog — the mechanism that makes a Bangladesh cold wave dangerous — is not a driver.
limits: No fog, no wind chill, no humidity: a dry 9 °C night and a foggy 9 °C night score the same.
BMD's own cold-wave criteria (which are station-based and use consecutive-day rules) are not what this proxy implements; the two can disagree, and this page says so rather than implying equivalence.

hazards.season: March–May, before the monsoon; also the December–January dry spell
hazards.summary: Vegetation and burn risk from heat, wind and drying.

physics.note: The three terms are heat, wind and drying — the fuel-moisture chain, not fire occurrence.

hazards.model: Classified from the same drivers. There is no active-fire input and no burnt-area input, so this class is a dryness-and-wind index wearing a hazard name, and the page says so.
hazards.confidence: Uncalibrated softmax; the confidence is the classifier's own certainty across the eight classes.
limits: No fuel load, no land cover, no ignition source, no thermal-anomaly feed (MODIS/VIIRS active fire is not ingested).
Rice-straw burning and brick-kiln seasonality are invisible to a district-aggregated weather index.
The class is retained because the model's vocabulary has eight classes and this is one of them — not because the pipeline measures fire.

hazards.season: March–May (Nor'wester / Kalbaishakhi), plus pre-monsoon squall lines
hazards.summary: Squall wind plus a convective downpour.

drivers: maximum wind in the horizon (W, km/h)
wettest 24 hours in that horizon (P_peak, mm)
physics.note: Uses the peak 24-hour rainfall rather than the horizon total, precisely so a wet fortnight is not read as a squall line — the defect the corrected wiring removed.

hazards.model: Classified from the same drivers; Severe Local Storm and Tropical Cyclone compete directly on the wind term and are separated by the rainfall pattern and the other drivers.
limits: No convective-available-potential-energy, no storm-top height, no hail: the meteorology that defines a Nor'wester is not an input.
Peak wind in a district aggregate understates the local maximum that damages a bazaar.
Hail and lightning — the two things that actually kill in a Kalbaishakhi — are not represented at all.

shared.physicsNotation: clip(x) clamps a term to [0, 1] — max(0, min(1, x)) — which is how every formula in the pipeline bounds its terms. Each term is clipped before it is weighted, so no single driver can run away with a score.
shared.classVocabulary: The eight classes above are the model's entire output vocabulary (`Models/labels.json`), enforced on ingest. A hazard outside the list is not mapped onto a nearest neighbour — an unrecognised label is rejected and reported.
shared.confidencePolicy: Confidence bins (Certain ≥ 0.85, Probable 0.70–0.85, Uncertain < 0.70) describe the model's own certainty in the class it chose. They are not accuracy, and no accuracy figure is published because no held-out evaluation has been run on real labels.
shared.publicationGate: Nothing above the WATCH level can be published automatically while no calibration map exists, and nothing at all can be published while the pipeline stamps no model version — the alert engine records that as `publication_blocked` rather than issuing the alert.
shared.groundTruth: Ground-truth reports (district, hazard, horizon, date, what was observed) are the only route by which this project can publish skill metrics. The contact page reaches the maintainers.
